The cheap-check plan (trust/rehash/purge) is unit-pinned. What is honestly NOT detectable in-session is measured and disclosed: docs/evidence/R2-3/env-probe.json shows this headless matrix reports persist()===false in EVERY Chromium context (persistent, incognito, ephemeral) and the same 10 GiB quota in incognito as in a normal profile — so persist() denial is recorded at the opt-in but never gates the offer, and a private window is not distinguishable from a first visit.

limitations: In-session, a wiped/private model store is NOT distinguishable from a first visit on this engine matrix (MEASURED, docs/evidence/R2-3/env-probe.json): Chromium headless reports persist()===false in EVERY context (persistent profile, incognito, ephemeral) and the same 10 GiB quota in incognito as in a normal profile, and a write/read probe succeeds everywhere in-session. The app therefore: requests persist() at the user's opt-in (recorded honestly; real browsers may grant it), refuses on the honest estimate bar (no-room), and shows the volatile refusal when the storage reports it cannot keep the model — the deterministic coverage is the test-build ?testStorage override (A29: absent from production). A real-device pass (A27) would measure real-Chrome incognito behaviour.

The volatile signal's production triggers (a real private window signature, a WebView wipe signal) are not observable with the APIs this matrix exposes; the policy and the refusal UI are wired and test-covered so a platform that reports the signal (e.g. a host app via R2-2's embedding) gets the kind refusal for free.

The fresh-start cheap check trusts the cache on size + the recorded sha256 marker; a marker that dies with a partially-evicted cache costs one 397 MB re-hash (by design, fail-closed), and corruption AFTER the marker was written is not re-detected at launch (the same trust model as every browser cache; the download itself always verifies before caching).

The existing download-flow specs open the Advanced section before the download click (a12/a13/a14/a21/eval/uc13/demo/a29, changed with the UI in this PR): the flows and assertions are otherwise unchanged.
Real installed-PWA / real-OS private-window behavior on the owner's devices stays NOT_RUN (A27, the plan's optional real-device pass; checklist in docs/KNOWN_LIMITS.md).
